clue.text: With "Eureka!" counter well hypothetical question

parts.note: Ha! is a cry of discovery, like Eureka!

indicators.note: counter means running the other way, so this word is read backwards

parts.note: well, as in in good health, means fit

explanation.surface: Someone shouts Eureka and then poses a speculative question about a well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well' looks like a water source but means in good health, and 'counter' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase introduces a supposition, the classic speculative question beginning a scenario.

clue.text: Facetious girl squeezes four couples in lift

indicators.note: squeezes means holds tightly inside

parts.note: hen is a jokey term for a woman or girl
four pairs make eight

explanation.surface: A jokey girl crams four couples into an elevator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lift' looks like the elevator but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to raise or increase.

clue.text: Can't he hold the binoculars steady?

definitions.text: Can't he hold the binoculars steady?

parts.words: Can't he hold the binoculars steady?
parts.note: a keen birdwatcher, whose name also suggests someone jittery

explanation.walkthrough: The British slang word for an obsessive birdwatcher also sounds like a person who jerks nervously.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for an avid birdwatcher chasing rare sightings, binoculars in hand.

clue.text: It's just as if RAF bombed Ireland

indicators.note: bombed means blown apart, so these letters are scattered

explanation.surface: An airborne raid on Ireland as if by the Royal Air Force.
explanation.walkthrough: RAF is the Royal Air Force.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom meaning the outcome is equitable, said when everyone has had an even deal.

clue.text: It's got a tablet for knocking back inside

definitions.text: It's got a tablet for knocking back inside

indicators.note: inside says these letters sit within the other word

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: knocking back, like downing a drink, here sends the word backwards

parts.note: a tablet is a pill

explanation.surface: A container holding a pill to be swallowed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for knocking back' sends the tablet backwards and 'inside' sets it within GOT; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A small earthenware apothecary's pot, the kind that might hold pills or ointment.

clue.text: "One doesn't usually admit them", orderly replies augustly

indicators.note: orderly suggests putting these letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A hospital orderly answers questions in a grand, dignified manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'orderly' looks like a hospital attendant but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Secret indulgences people enjoy but are embarrassed to confess to.

clue.text: Left here as before, I departed son's party

indicators.note: departed means left, so this letter goes

parts.note: ibidem is Latin for in the same place, cited earlier
S is an abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a son's party early.
explanation.walkthrough: Liberal Democrats are a UK political party.
explanation.definitionFit: A British political grouping, the Liberal Democrats, abbreviated.

clue.text: Hang out with Henry in pub, on the beer — one of quite a few in hand!

definitions.text: one of quite a few in hand

parts.note: PH is the map abbreviation for public house

indicators.note: on as in on the beer, sitting within the drink

parts.note: ale is beer

indicators.note: out with means this letter is cast out

parts.note: taken as written
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Someone hangs out with Henry at the pub, drinking heavily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out with' drops Henry's letter; 'on' reads as 'on the beer', inside the drink. PH marks a pub on British maps.
explanation.definitionFit: A finger or toe bone; the hand contains fourteen of them.

clue.text: Extremely desirable editor of Nuts!

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so these letters go wild

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic editor of a men's magazine, Nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: Nuts was a British men's weekly magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for something so desirable one would make any sacrifice for it.

clue.text: Current rent in arrears, again — this will give big buddy thrills!

definitions.text: this will give big buddy thrills

indicators.note: again says the reversed group is written a second time
in arrears means behind, so the pair is read from the back

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current
rent, as a noun, is a rip or tear

explanation.surface: A financial plea about rent overdue, oddly ending in excitement for a large friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in arrears' turns I RIP into PIRI; 'again' doubles it. 'big buddy' plays on taste buds being thrilled by the hot sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiery chilli sauce excites the taste buds, the playful 'buddy' of the clue.

clue.text: A winner at Eisteddfod penning Love at Sea?

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the chief prize at the Welsh Eisteddfod festival goes to a bard
love is zero in tennis, so the letter O

explanation.surface: A Welsh festival champion writes a romance titled Love at Sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The Eisteddfod is a Welsh festival of poetry and music whose top honour is the bard's chair.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on a ship at sea means being on board, phrased as a playful question.

clue.text: Solidly built but stupid group of people

parts.note: thick is slang for stupid
a set is a circle or group of people

explanation.surface: A description of a hefty but dim crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a stocky, heavily built physique.

clue.text: Got suited

definitions.meaning: got as in turned into, as in grew angry
suited as in flattered, a dress that looks good on someone

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: to turn into something, and to look good on someone.

clue.text: Like, perhaps, for one to illustrate four of them?

definitions.text: Like, perhaps, for one to illustrate four of them?

parts.words: Like, perhaps, for one to illustrate four of them?
parts.note: Like, perhaps, for one, and to illustrate are four phrases each introducing an instance

explanation.surface: A self-referential question about four phrases.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue itself contains four introducers of instances, so it illustrates the very thing it asks for.
explanation.definitionFit: Instances or illustrations, each flagged by phrases like those in the clue.

clue.text: Radical not entirely negligent in falling off the wagon?

indicators.note: in says this piece is placed within the other

parts.note: falling off the wagon is no longer teetotal: ex-TT

indicators.note: not entirely means a letter is chopped off the end

parts.note: remiss means negligent

explanation.surface: A careless drinker who has lapsed back into the bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: TT means teetotal; 'falling off the wagon' makes someone ex-TT. 'not entirely' cuts REMISS to REMIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone holding radical views, a zealot.

clue.text: Expert nicker …

definitions.meaning: an expert, someone very skilled at something, in British slang
nicker is British slang for a pound, a one-pound coin or note

explanation.walkthrough: 'nicker' looks like a thief but is slang for a pound sterling.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang: a skilled person, and also a single pound, both British colloquialisms.

clue.text: Couple's turn to describe future without following up

indicators.note: to describe is to draw around, so this piece encloses the rest
turn says the word is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: a duo is a couple

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so this piece wraps the letter

parts.note: to be describes what is in the future, as in the bride-to-be
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: A pair take turns describing a future with no follow-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, and 'to describe' means to draw round. The tiny 'up' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: risen for the day, no longer lying down.

clue.text: Bind over Hercules, perhaps on sixth of Labours, offering unavoidable choice

indicators.note: over in a down clue means turned upside down, so read backwards

parts.note: to bind is to tie
Hercules is an example of a hero

indicators.note: sixth of picks the sixth letter of the word

explanation.surface: A legal binding-over order on Hercules after his sixth labour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns TIE into EIT; 'sixth of' takes R from Labours.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes a dilemma where one must pick one of two alternatives.

clue.text: … covering face when moving around a close

indicators.note: moving around says the trimmed word goes about the next letter
the covering face is the front letter, which is lost from the word

parts.note: the ellipsis carries on from the previous clue, whose nicker is a pound coin

explanation.surface: Continues the story of the thief, hiding his face as he moves close.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis picks up 15's answer, ONER; 'covering face' drops its first letter to leave NER, and 'moving around' puts that round A.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: nearby, close at hand.

clue.text: There's little thought in this all-points bulletin, going over the top

indicators.note: going over in a down clue places one piece above another

parts.note: news is a bulletin; all points are N, E, W and S of the compass
a peak is the top

explanation.surface: A police all-points bulletin going over the top.
explanation.walkthrough: The Orwellian language of Nineteen Eighty-Four, designed to narrow thought.
explanation.definitionFit: Orwell's invented language in Nineteen Eighty-Four was built to restrict thinking.

clue.text: Capital, like "C" in "Confederation"

parts.note: as means like

indicators.note: in places the letter within the word

parts.note: a union is a confederation
taken as written

explanation.surface: A capital letter, like C in Confederation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' suggests an upper-case letter, but it is a city.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of Paraguay.

clue.text: Person who's been taken in meets errand-boy on return

indicators.note: on return says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone detained meets an errand-boy on the way back.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone taken into custody by police, a detainee.

clue.text: Twit's big bird bandaged with help

indicators.note: bandaged with means wrapped round by

parts.note: aid is help
the rhea is a large flightless South American bird

explanation.surface: A large bird is bandaged up with assistance.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a silly, empty-headed person.

clue.text: Interior of gift to Troy secretes the people not yet accounted for

indicators.note: secretes means hides away, so one piece is tucked inside
interior of means only the inside, so the outer letters are stripped

parts.note: the wooden horse left by the Greeks was the gift to Troy
taken as written

explanation.surface: The Trojan horse hides the soldiers no one has yet counted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Interior of' leaves ORS from HORSE; it 'secretes' THE.
explanation.definitionFit: The rest, the remaining people still to be reckoned with.

clue.text: Felt covers of Let it Be and Help! inspired Lennon finally

parts.note: stet is the proofreader's mark meaning let it stand

indicators.note: inspired means breathed in, so a letter is taken inside

parts.note: SOS is the distress call for help

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Beatles album covers, Let It Be and Help!, inspired by Lennon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Felt covers' are hats made of felt. 'finally' gives N, which SOS 'inspired'.
explanation.definitionFit: Wide-brimmed cowboy hats are traditionally made of felt and cover the head.

clue.text: Composer gets in during shouting-match

indicators.note: gets in says this piece goes inside the next

parts.note: by means during, as in by night
Thomas Arne was the English composer of Rule, Britannia!

explanation.surface: A composer joins in a slanging match.
explanation.definitionFit: British colloquial word for a noisy quarrel or row.

clue.text: Stopped anti-Loyalist returning?

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: a Loyalist backs Northern Ireland's union with Britain; an opponent is an NI denier

explanation.surface: A republican campaigner is halted on coming home.
explanation.walkthrough: NI is Northern Ireland; Loyalists support its union with Britain, so its opponent is pictured as an 'NI denier'.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: held back or checked, like a horse pulled up by its reins.

clue.text: They mock retarded revolutionaries, southern island captured

indicators.note: retarded means held back, so the letters run backwards
captured says one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: Reds are revolutionaries, communists; two of them here
the second red revolutionary

explanation.surface: Scoffers sneer at slow radicals who have seized a southern island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'captured' puts I between RED and RED; 'retarded' turns REDIRED into DERIDER, then S follows.
explanation.definitionFit: People who ridicule or scoff, those who sneer.

clue.text: Kleptomania is by definition this infectious

definitions.meaning: kleptomania is a compulsion to steal, i.e. to help oneself
infectious in the dated sense of catching

explanation.definitionFit: Stealing is helping oneself; and an old word for catching, as of a disease.
